novelty.justification: The claim proposes a measurement-level hypothesis that a backdoor creates a "paraphrase-invariance violation" in activation space, where a trigger-crossing paraphrase "jumps to an anomalous region." Searches around "LLM backdoor detection semantic-preserving paraphrases hidden-state activations," "trigger-agnostic backdoor paraphrase consistency," and "activation discontinuity backdoor detection" identify Preference Instability in Reward Models (2026) as the closest work because it already studies representation-level instability under paraphrasing and backdoor triggers, while Trap on Text (2026) detects activated backdoors through responses to semantic perturbations and Hidden State Forensics (2025) detects LLM attacks from activation anomalies. Moving from those results to residual-stream outliers over paraphrase clouds in generative text LLMs is a natural extension and non-trivial combination, particularly for model-level screening, but it does not require an entirely new core relationship because semantic perturbation inconsistency and latent separability of triggered inputs are already established.
